author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacted to Barack Obama's speech at Stanford calling for more censorship to combat misinformation, arguing Obama functions as a convenient mouthpiece for centralized power, alongside figures like Tony Blair and Yuval Noah Harari. He explained the goal isn't necessarily to make people believe specific lies, but to flood public discourse with enough noise and conspiracy that citizens stop knowing what to trust at all. He pushed back hard on Obama comparing independent media to raw sewage, calling it brilliant rhetoric precisely because ongoing public debate means centralized institutions can no longer fully control the narrative. Russell argued the real message is simple: when Obama talks about who needs to be censored, he means voices like his, and like yours.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacted to a news segment where a reporter pressed him on whether setting a car on fire should land someone in jail, then followed up asking if that applied to "any car," which Russell found almost too absurd to take seriously. He poked fun at how self-important mainstream news has become, pointing out most of what gets treated as urgent, serious television is really just jibber jabber dressed up as importance. He took the bit even further, joking about whether the same standard should apply to setting a mouse on fire, and whether you could even drive one.

description:

The conversation explores whether reclaiming those fundamentals could change far more than where we live.

description:

title: Are we already in a holy war?

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell argued the real crisis of our time is centralized power, pointing to unelected bureaucracies like the WHO, NATO, the UN and the EU, alongside NGOs and deep state influence, as forces that obscure themselves while making decisions on a global scale, all while elected governments take the public blame. He said most people can feel that power has migrated away from them, that sovereignty over their own lives and communities has quietly disappeared, even while some insist things have never been better. His guest agreed without hesitation, adding that a person can become materially richer while growing spiritually poorer at the exact same time.
